Advanced Solution

Why Zygomatic Implants Transform Impossible Cases

Zygomatic implants are specialized titanium fixtures anchored in the dense cheekbone (zygoma) rather than the jaw. They’re the gold standard for patients with severe upper jaw bone loss who would otherwise need extensive bone grafting.

No Bone Grafting

Zygomatic implants bypass the atrophied upper jaw entirely by anchoring into the cheekbone — which never resorbs. This eliminates 6–12 months of bone graft healing and multiple surgeries, saving time and avoiding graft complications.

Immediate Function

Temporary teeth are attached the same day as surgery — you walk out with a full smile. The dense zygomatic bone provides immediate primary stability, allowing for functional loading within 24–48 hours unlike traditional grafting protocols.

Superior Anchorage

The zygomatic bone is 3–4 times denser than maxillary bone. This exceptional density provides rock-solid implant stability and reduces risk of early failure. Zygomatic implants routinely achieve higher insertion torque values than conventional implants.

Suitable for Extreme Cases

Zygomatic implants are designed for patients with <5mm of residual bone — cases where conventional implants and even sinus lifts are impossible. They're the last-resort solution that works when nothing else can.

Cost-Effective at Scale

While zygomatic implants cost more than conventional ones, they’re far cheaper than the alternative: multiple sinus lifts + bone grafts + conventional implants. Total treatment time is also 6–9 months shorter, reducing overall expenses.

Proven Long-Term Success

Clinical studies confirm 95–97% survival rates at 10+ years. The technique was pioneered in the 1990s and has decades of documented outcomes. Zygomatic implants are no longer experimental — they’re mainstream for severe bone loss cases.

Advanced Anatomy

How Zygomatic Implants Work

Zygomatic implants bypass the atrophied upper jaw by anchoring directly into the dense cheekbone (zygomatic arch), providing stable support for full arch restorations without bone grafting.

1

Zygomatic Bone Anchor

Dense cheekbone provides superior anchorage — never resorbs unlike jaw bone

2

Extra-Long Implants

40–55mm titanium fixtures traverse sinus and anchor in zygoma at 45° angle

3

Bypasses Atrophied Jaw

Eliminates need for sinus lifts or bone grafts in patients with <5mm residual bone

4

Combined Configuration

Typically 2–4 zygomatic + 2–4 conventional anterior implants per arch for optimal support

Treatment Journey

Your Zygomatic Implant Procedure

From consultation to final prosthesis — the entire journey typically requires two visits to Istanbul over 5–6 months.

1
Pre-Arrival

Specialized Planning

Before you travel, VeaHealth coordinates advanced diagnostics — high-resolution CBCT scan showing zygomatic anatomy, sinus positioning, and nerve pathways. A specialized zygomatic surgeon designs your implant trajectory virtually.

  • Medical history & video consultation
  • High-res 3D CBCT scan analyzed
  • Zygomatic trajectory planning software
  • Combined zygoma + conventional plan
  • Travel & hotel coordination
2
Day 1–2 — Istanbul

Zygomatic Surgery

Under general anesthesia, 2–4 zygomatic implants are placed per arch using 3D-guided navigation. The extra-long implants traverse the sinus and anchor in the cheekbone. Temporary teeth are attached immediately.

  • General anesthesia or IV sedation
  • Tooth extractions if needed
  • 2–4 zygomatic implants placed (40–55mm)
  • 2–4 conventional anterior implants
  • Same-day temporary prosthesis attached
3
Day 3–10 — Istanbul

Recovery & Monitoring

You remain in Istanbul for 7–10 days for close monitoring. Swelling peaks at 72 hours. Your surgeon verifies implant stability and adjusts temporary teeth. Post-op care is more intensive than conventional implants due to sinus proximity.

  • Daily clinic check-ups
  • Suture removal (day 10–14)
  • Nasal decongestants prescribed
  • Bite adjustment on temporary teeth
  • Pain management closely monitored
4
Month 1–4

Osseointegration

Implants fuse with zygomatic bone over 4–6 months. You wear temporary teeth during this period and gradually resume normal eating. VeaHealth monitors your healing remotely via photos, video calls, and symptom tracking.

  • Bone integration in zygoma
  • Temporary teeth remain functional
  • Gradual diet progression
  • Remote monitoring every 2 weeks
  • No travel required during healing
5
Month 5–6 — Return Visit

Final Prosthesis

You return to Istanbul for 3–5 days. The temporary bridge is removed and digital impressions are taken. Your final premium zirconia prosthesis is fabricated, tested for fit and occlusion, and permanently attached.

  • Temporary prosthesis removed
  • Digital impressions & bite registration
  • Final zirconia bridge crafted (2–3 days)
  • Try-in with shade and occlusion check
  • Permanent screw-retention & warranty docs

Patient Questions

Frequently Asked Questions

Are zygomatic implants safe?

Yes. Zygomatic implants have been used since 1998 with well-documented safety profiles. The procedure is more complex than conventional implants and requires a specialized surgeon, but serious complications are rare (<2%). Mild, self-limiting sinusitis is the most common issue (10.5% of cases).

Is zygomatic implant surgery painful?

The procedure is performed under general anesthesia — you feel nothing during surgery. Post-op discomfort (swelling, nasal congestion, soreness) is more significant than conventional implants and peaks at 72 hours. Pain is managed with prescription medications and typically resolves within 10–14 days.

How long do zygomatic implants last?

The titanium fixtures can last a lifetime with proper care — studies confirm 95%+ survival at 10 years and documented cases exceeding 20 years. The zirconia prosthesis may need replacement after 15–20 years due to wear. Biannual check-ups are essential for long-term success.

Am I a candidate for zygomatic implants?

Zygomatic implants are designed for patients with severe upper jaw bone loss — typically <5mm of residual bone where conventional implants and sinus lifts are impossible. VeaHealth's surgeons assess eligibility during the 3D CBCT scan consultation. Not all severe bone loss cases require zygomatic implants.

How many trips to Istanbul are required?

Two visits: the first for surgery and temporary teeth (7–10 days due to more intensive monitoring), and a second visit 5–6 months later for the final prosthesis (3–5 days). The healing phase in between is managed remotely by VeaHealth.

Will I have sinus problems after zygomatic implants?

Mild, temporary sinusitis occurs in ~10% of patients and resolves with antibiotics and decongestants within 2–4 weeks. The implants traverse the sinus but don’t cause chronic sinus issues. Serious complications like sinus perforation or chronic infection are rare (<2%) with experienced surgeons.

What implant brand will be used?

VeaHealth exclusively uses Straumann and Nobel Biocare zygomatic implants — the two brands with the most clinical validation for this advanced technique. The specific brand, model, and serial numbers are documented in your treatment file and provided at completion.

Is the warranty valid internationally?

Yes. VeaHealth’s lifetime warranty on zygomatic implants and 3-year warranty on prosthetics are valid worldwide. If a warranty issue arises after you return home, VeaHealth coordinates resolution remotely or via a local affiliated specialist clinic in your country.
